lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to World 16, the Ruins of Memory. Last time, the wind feather showed us old stone ruins on the map. And now we are here! Look at these old walls and this tall tower. Long, long ago, people lived here. Today's sentence is: People lived here long ago. Say it with me. People lived here long ago. Great! Lived is the past form of live. We use past forms for things that already happened. このワールドでは「すぎた こと」を たくさん はなすよ。 Long ago means a very long time before now. Now, phonics. Live, lived. Like, liked. Dance, danced. Smile, smiled. These words end in e, so we just add d. Easy, right? Here's a tip. Ruins are very old and easy to break, so we touch them gently. Let's be careful explorers. Ready? Let's explore the ruins!

segments.say: Sound time! Words ending in E? Just add D. Live, lived. Like, liked. Dance, danced. Smile, smiled. Lived ends with a soft d, liked with a quick t.

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! We're at the entrance of the ruins. Before we go in, let's talk about yesterday. To ask about yesterday, say, What did you do yesterday? Say it with me. What did you do yesterday? Great! Did is the past form of do. In the answer, we use a past form. I played soccer with my friends. I tried a new food. It was good! きのうの ことは did で きいて、played の ような すぎた かたちで こたえるよ。 Now, phonics. Cry, cried. Try, tried. Carry, carried. Study, studied. When a word ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i and add ed. Let's spell cried together. C, r, i, e, d. Good! Here's a tip. When your friend answers, ask one more question, like, Was it fun? Then it's a real conversation. OK, let's ask our friends about yesterday!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're in a long, dark passage in the ruins. Shh! What was that? Something moved! To ask a friend, say, Did you see that? Say it with me. Did you see that? Good! For a yes answer, say, Yes, I did. For a no answer, say, No, I didn't. Didn't means did not. Did ～? の しつもんには、Yes, I did. か No, I didn't. で こたえるよ。 Let's try one more. Did you hear a noise? No, I didn't. Now, phonics. Today we mix all the rules. Jump, jumped. Just add ed. Wave, waved. Just add d. Hug, hugged. Double the g. Hurry, hurried. Change y to i. Here's a tip. If you see a small wild animal, don't touch it. Just watch it quietly. OK, let's find out what moved!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Our first day at the ruins is over. Tonight, let's write a ruins diary in the tent. In a diary, we write about things that already happened, so we use past forms. Today's sentences are: We walked to the ruins. We found a door. Say them with me. We walked to the ruins. We found a door. Great! Walked has ed, but found is a special past form. Find, found. 日記は すぎた ことだから、すぎた かたちで かくよ。 You can also use was and were. It was dark, but we weren't scared. Weren't means were not. Now, phonics review. Walked. Arrived. Clapped. Carried. Remember the four ed rules! Here's a tip. In a diary for sharing, you don't need to write your real name or address. OK, let's read our diaries to each other!

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! Last night, we all made a campfire together in the plaza. Do you remember? Today's sentence is: We sang a song by the campfire. Say it with me. We sang a song by the campfire. Wonderful! Sang is the past form of sing. Some verbs don't use ed. They change their spelling instead. sing の すぎた かたちは singed では なく、sang だよ。 Now, phonics. Sing, sang. Swim, swam. Drink, drank. Ring, rang. Can you hear it? The i changes to a. Let's say them again quickly. Sang, swam, drank, rang! Great! You can also ask a friend, Did you sing, too? Yes, I did. Here's a tip. A campfire is very hot, so always make one with a grown-up. Never play with fire. OK, let's talk about our campfire night!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Look, there's an old mailbox near the ruins. And it still works! Last night, Riko wrote a letter. Today's sentence is: I wrote a letter to my grandma. Say it with me. I wrote a letter to my grandma. Great! Wrote is the past form of write. It's a special one, with no ed. A letter starts with Dear. Dear Grandma. And it often ends with Love, and your name. てがみの はじめは Dear ～, だよ。 Now, phonics. Begin, began. Give, gave. Sink, sank. Drink, drank. The i changes to a again. Here's a tip. On an envelope, we write an address. But on the internet or in a chat, never share your address. That's a safety rule. OK, who will you write to? Let's write a short letter!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we met the guide of the ruins. I'll play the guide's daughter, Sana. Let's talk about last weekend. To ask, say, Where did you go last weekend? Say it with me. Where did you go last weekend? Great! To answer, use went. Went is the past form of go. I went to the beach with my family. If you didn't go anywhere, that's OK. Say, I stayed home and read a book. どこにも いかなかった ときは I stayed home. で いいよ。 Let's practice. Where did you go last weekend? I went to the zoo. Sounds fun! Now, phonics. Give, gave. Drink, drank. Swim, swam. Sink, sank. The i changes to a. Here's a tip. After the answer, ask one more question, like, Was it fun? OK, let's talk about our weekends!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're taking a break at the rest area of the ruins. Let's have a weekend talk. Today's sentences are: I went to the river. I caught a fish. Say them with me. I went to the river. I caught a fish. Great! Caught is the past form of catch. We'll learn more about it later. To keep talking, a friend can ask, What did you do there? Then answer with two or three past sentences. 2〜3文で はなすと、ほんとうの かいわに なるよ。 And add your feeling. It was exciting! Let's try. What did you do there? I played with my dog. It was fun! Now, phonics review. Swam. Sang. Stopped. Tried. Do you remember the rules? Here's a tip. Near a river, always stay with a grown-up, and don't go into deep water. OK, let's share our weekends!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! There's a souvenir shop near the gate of the ruins. Souvenirs are things you buy on a trip to remember it. Today's sentence is: I bought a map at the shop. Say it with me. I bought a map at the shop. Great! Bought is the past form of buy. Buy, bought. It looks very different! To ask a friend, say, What did you buy? buy の すぎた かたちは bought。かたちが ぜんぜん ちがうね。 Now, phonics. Today we learn a new pattern. Write, wrote. Ride, rode. Drive, drove. Rise, rose. The i changes to o, and the word still ends with magic e. So the o says its name. Here's a tip. When you buy something, look at the clerk and say thank you. OK, let's go shopping!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we visit a pot maker's workshop at the ruins. Ms. Emma will play the pot maker. Look at these beautiful old patterns. To ask who taught someone, say, Who taught you? Say it with me. Who taught you? Great! Taught is the past form of teach. To answer, say, My grandpa taught me. Or say it short, My grandpa did. Who ～? の こたえは「～ did.」と みじかく いっても いいよ。 Let's practice. Who taught you? My mom taught me. My mom did. Now, phonics. Know, knew. Grow, grew. Throw, threw. Blow, blew. The past form ends in ew. It sounds like oo, as in moon. Here's a tip. When someone teaches you something, say, Thank you for teaching me! Let's say it. Thank you for teaching me! OK, let's ask the pot maker!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Look up. Can you see the top of the tower? There are one hundred stairs! Let's climb. Today's sentence is: It wasn't easy, but I did it. Say it with me. It wasn't easy, but I did it. Great! Wasn't means was not. You can use this sentence for things that were hard for you. You can also ask, Were you tired? Yes, I was. Or, No, I wasn't. was / were の いいえは wasn't / weren't だよ。 Now, phonics. Fly, flew. Draw, drew. Throw, threw. Grow, grew. The past form ends in ew again. Here's a tip. On high stairs, hold the rail and never push your friends. Go one step at a time. OK, let's climb carefully and talk about hard things we did!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we found a big stone with old words on it. It's a story! Many stories start with Once upon a time. It means long, long ago. むかしむかし、と おなじ いみだよ。 Today's sentence is: Once upon a time, a king lived here. Say it with me. Once upon a time, a king lived here. Wonderful! Let's read on. He had a big castle, but he was lonely. One day, a little bird brought him a box. One day is another good story word. Now, phonics. Buy, bought. Think, thought. Bring, brought. Fight, fought. These past forms have ought. The g and h are silent. Here's a tip. When you listen to a story, make pictures in your head. OK, let's read the story on the stone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Let's read more of the king's story. Stories happen in order, so we use special words to show the order. First. Then. After that. Today's sentences are: First, he opened the box. Then, he looked inside. Say them with me. First, he opened the box. Then, he looked inside. Great! What did he find? A tiny seed! After that, he planted the seed. じゅんばんを あらわす ことばを つかうと、おはなしが わかりやすく なるよ。 Let's say the order words again. First. Then. After that. To ask about a story, say, What happened next? Now, phonics. Catch, caught. Teach, taught. Buy, bought. Think, thought. Caught and taught have aught. Bought and thought have ought. They sound the same! Here's a tip. Remember the cooking class in World 14? We said First and Next. Stories use order words, too! OK, let's read on!

The king brought them apples from the tree. Today's sentence is: Finally, the king smiled. Say it with me. Finally, the king smiled. Great! Finally means at the end. We use it for the last part of a story. Finally は「さいごに」。おはなしの おわりに つかうよ。 He wasn't lonely anymore. The end! Let's say the last part again together. Finally, the king smiled. The end! Now, phonics. Bring, brought. Fight, fought. Catch, caught. Teach, taught. Ought or aught? Look carefully at the spelling. Here's a tip. A good story ending makes people feel something. Happy, surprised, or warm inside. OK, let's finish the story!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Let's think about the king's feelings. To ask, say, How did he feel? Say it with me. How did he feel? Good! Felt is the past form of feel. He felt sad. He felt surprised. He felt happy. You can add a reason with because. He felt sad because he was lonely. きもちと りゆうを いえると、おはなしが もっと ふかく わかるよ。 At the start, he felt sad. At the end, he felt happy. Feelings can change in a story. Let's practice. How did she feel? She felt happy because she won the race. Now, phonics. Think, thought. Catch, caught. Buy, bought. Teach, taught. Let's say them fast. Thought, caught, bought, taught! Here's a tip. Thinking about feelings in stories helps us be kind to real people, too. OK, let's talk about feelings!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Tonight is story time in the plaza of the ruins. Each of us will tell a short story. Use these story words. Once upon a time. First. Then. After that. Finally. Today's sentence is: Once upon a time, a little dragon lived in the tower. Say it with me. Once upon a time, a little dragon lived in the tower. Great! First, it flew to the river. Then, it met a fish. Finally, they became best friends. Your story can be about anything. An animal, a robot, or a magic tree. おはなしの なかみは じゆう。すきな ものを だしてね。 Now, phonics review. Thought. Caught. Rode. Knew. Here's a tip. When a friend tells a story, listen quietly and clap at the end. OK, who wants to go first?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we meet a traveler at the ruins. Birimo will play the traveler, Leo. Let's talk about summer vacation. To ask, say, How was your summer? Say it with me. How was your summer? Great! To answer, say, It was great! Or, It was fun! Then add one more sentence about what you did. I went to the mountains. And then ask back, How about you? How about you? と ききかえすと、かいわが つづくよ。 Now, phonics. Today, let's listen to the sounds of ed. Played. The ed sounds like d. Jumped. It sounds like t. Wanted. It sounds like id. Enjoyed. It sounds like d. Here's a tip. When you say jumped, the ed is short and quiet. Don't say jump-ed! OK, let's share our summer stories!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we talked about summer. Today, let's ask more questions to learn more. These are called follow-up questions. One good question is, Who did you go with? Say it with me. Who did you go with? Great! The answer can be short. With my family. With my friends. Another question is, How long did you stay? For three days. もう ひとつ しつもんを すると、あいての はなしが もっと よく わかるよ。 Let's practice. Who did you go with? With my friends. How long did you stay? For two days. Now, phonics. Listen to the ed sounds. Visited, id. Stayed, d. Walked, t. Laughed, t. In laughed, g h sounds like f, and the ed sounds like t. Here's a tip. Ask questions because you are interested, and listen to the answers with a smile. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Good listeners react to stories. Today, let's learn two reactions. For a happy story, say, Sounds fun! Say it with me. Sounds fun! For a bad story, say, Oh no! What happened? Say it with me. Oh no! What happened? Great! たのしい はなしには Sounds fun! こまった はなしには Oh no! だよ。 Then you can ask, Are you OK now? Yes, I'm fine. Let's practice. I lost my pencil case yesterday. Oh no! What happened? I went to the zoo with my class. Sounds fun! Wonderful reactions! Now, phonics. Listen to the ed sounds. Dropped, t. Cried, d. Shouted, id. Missed, t. Here's a tip. Everyone makes mistakes. When a friend shares a funny mistake, don't laugh at them. Laugh with them. OK, let's tell our stories and react!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're reporters. Let's do a memory interview. To ask about the time, say, When did you learn to ride a bike? Say it with me. When did you learn to ride a bike? Great! Answers can be short. Last year. When I was five. Then ask, How was it? It was hard at first. And then, How was it in the end? It was great! いつ？ どうだった？ と きくと、おもいでの はなしが ひろがるよ。 Let's practice once more. When did you learn to swim? When I was six. How was it? It was fun! Now, phonics review. Asked. Worried. Nodded. Smiled. Do you remember the four ed rules? Here's a tip. In an interview, you don't need to say your real name. Just have fun and listen well. OK, let's start the interview!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Do you remember the key we found at the top of the tower? Today we found a treasure box for it! But the box has a password. To open it, we must say past forms. Today's sentence is: I went, I saw, I ate, I bought. Say it with me. I went, I saw, I ate, I bought. Great! Go, went. See, saw. Eat, ate. Buy, bought. These past forms are special. ed を つけない とくべつな かたちだよ。 Remember, we don't say goed or eated. Those words are not English. Let's try more. Sing, sang. Know, knew. Write, wrote. Now, phonics review. Bought. Sang. Knew. Wrote. Let's say them fast! Here's a tip. Make past form cards and play a game with your family. OK, let's open the treasure box!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! In the treasure box, we found an old diary. A child wrote it long ago. Let's read it. Today, I helped my mother. We made bread. Then I played by the big tree. The king waved to me. I was happy. Now, let's write our own diary pages. Today's sentence is: Last Sunday, I went to the library. It was quiet. Say it with me. Last Sunday, I went to the library. It was quiet. Great! Write three or four sentences. When was it? Where did you go? What did you do? How did you feel? いつ・どこ・なにを した・きもち の じゅんに かこう。 Now, phonics review. Visited. Studied. Swam. Gave. Here's a tip. You don't need to write your real name or address. OK, let's write!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! This is our last tour of the Ruins of Memory. Let's look back at everything we did. Ask your friends, What did you do at the ruins? Where did you go first? Did you like it? Say it with me. What did you do at the ruins? Great! Remember these question starters. What did. Where did. Who did. And How was. They help you talk about the past. すぎた ことを きく しつもんを ぜんぶ つかってみよう。 Let's practice. Where did you go first? I went to the tower. Did you like it? Yes, I did! Now, phonics review. Stopped. Began. Rode. lessons.teacherScript: Congratulations, everyone! This is the last lesson of World 16. ワールド16 さいごの レッスンだよ。 First, speed challenge! Look! Stop! Come here! Go! Sing! Swim! Write! Fly! Great! Now, it's the World 16 story show in the plaza. Today's sentence is: Once upon a time, four friends found a map. Say it with me. Once upon a time, four friends found a map. Wonderful! A good story uses order words. First. Then. After that. Finally. And it uses past forms. Walked. Found. Opened. Smiled. Now, the last phonics review. Lived. Sang. Flew. Thought. Wrote. Amazing! And look, the old diary has one more page. It's a map of the stars! Where are we going next? But first, your story show. Speak loudly and smile. You can do it!
